messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about one‑tenth of an atmosphere), pure water’s freezing (melting) point drops only modestly from its standard value of 0 °C at 101.3 kPa. Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the solid–liquid transition and the known latent heat of fusion for water, the calculated freezing point at 10 kPa is roughly:

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \approx -2^{\circ}\text{C}
\]

So you can expect water to freeze at about **–2 °C** when the ambient pressure is reduced to 10 kPa.
